name: Nimitz-class aircraft carrier, drawn as USS Ronald Reagan (CVN-76), 2003-04

published.source: en.wikipedia 'Nimitz-class aircraft carrier': length 1,092 ft (332.8 m) overall, beam 252 ft (76.8 m) flight deck, 134 ft (40.8 m) waterline, draught 37 ft (11.3 m)

references.name: [T1] USS Theodore Roosevelt (CVN-71) 1986, starboard beam, from a little above
references.source: Wikimedia Commons 'A starboard beam view of the nuclear-powered aircraft carrier USS THEODORE ROOSEVELT (CVN 71) underway - DPLA - da85f279b68fda546efbfe8777a1c8e8.jpeg' (US Navy / NARA), thumb 1600 x 1033
references.note: Scaled on the published 332.8 m flight deck: round-down end x 159, deck tip x 1397.5 (1238.5 px, 3.722 px/m), so model x 0 falls at x 778.3; waterline about row 423 (420 at the stern, 424 at the stem). Taken from a little above the horizontal (the deck shows, the far deck edge stands a few px high) and not long-lens; the deck height (rows 357..423, 17.7 m) reads low, hence exact false. The landmark tolerance is 2 m because the measured errors against the drawing are 0.75 to 1.85 m with MIXED signs (photo minus model: lift 3 after edge -1.85, lift 2 -0.75 / +0.95, lift 1 after edge +1.75, sponson ends -1.7 / +1.4, whip -1.1): reading noise on a soft 3.72 px/m photograph, about 7 px, not a systematic spread or a shape error. The same hull as Reagan, but the 1980s island and lattice mast: the island is NOT measured on it for this row. The window stops at the deck (z 20.5): above it the backdrop is sea, which the bg mask cannot tell from the grey island, so only the hull is compared.

must_show: angled deck 9 deg to port, its outboard edge straight at y 38.2..40.5 from x -124.5 to 61, cut back on a long diagonal from (61, 40.5) to (89, 18.6)
four deck-edge lifts raised flush: three to starboard at x 8.8..34.7, -36.6..-10.7, -116.5..-90.6 (y -20.9..-36.8), one on the port quarter at x -157.6..-131.6
hangar openings cut through the starboard side under each lift, hangar deck z 7.0 to head z 15.4, the hangar's deck, far bulkhead and overhead frames showing

island block x -71..-41 at y -38..-28 (roof of the block z 27.2), three glazed tiers, the heavy three-yard tower mast at x -56.5 (yards z 45.4, 50.0, 54.4, masthead z 66.9), SPS-48E forward on its pedestal at x -45.8 and the SPS-49 on the after platform at x -67.2
white SATCOM domes: the big pair on the forward roof corners at x -44.8, smaller ones at x -70.0, -62.0 and -67.6
low forward starboard sponson x 89..111 at z 14.8 with its box launcher at x 101.5; forward port sponson x 60..92 under the diagonal with RAM at x 84
deck-edge whip aerials on hinged feet at the end of outriggers from the catwalks: starboard x -130, -5, 45 and the tall one at x 72 (to z 32.4), port x -60, 0, 40

catwalks, safety nets (inboard edge on the catwalk, frame tube outboard) and life-raft racks round every deck edge at z 17.8..18.5; guard rails with stanchions and a mid wire round every platform and yard
four catapult tracks (two up the bow at x 62..160.5, two in the waist from x -40.5 to 57), three arresting pendants on the landing area at landing-axis stations -104.0, -91.8, -79.6
raked, flared bow over a bulb (stem at the waterline about x 159), narrow square stern with the open fantail under the round-down at x -163

not_confirmed: Reagan's island, tower mast and dome layout follow the 2004 photographs taken from her PORT quarter (US Navy 040723-N-7615S-305, 040621-N-6536T-066) and the 2005 bow view; no broadside of CVN-76 was found, so none of it is measured to scale

[T1] (TR 1986) reads the 1980s island block x -68.0..-42.6 against -71..-41 drawn, the stem meeting the water near x 151 against 155.7 (159 with Reagan's bulb), and lift 1's forward edge at 38.0 against 34.7; the shot is from above and read to about 7 px, so the drawing keeps the stations of the earlier, finer reading
the bulb itself (under water in every photograph)
the stations of the deck-edge whips other than the tall one at x 72: the one formerly drawn at x -20 stood on lift 2 and is now at x -5, clear of the raft rack at x -2.7..0.8
the outriggers and hinged feet of the whips (the photographs are too small to show how they are carried; drawn as the class's lowering whips are usually rigged)
lift outlines drawn square, lift 4 drawn raised
